summary: Project duplication now runs on the ArcRho Server host with live reserving-class progress.
details: The desktop app submits an asynchronous copy job instead of copying the project across the client network drive.
ArcRho Engine runs the copy on a bounded background worker so ordinary calculation requests can continue while a large project is duplicated.
A shell-owned progress window shows preparation, reserving-class copy counts, and finalization while the job runs.
Project Settings saves a client request ID before submission, safely replays uncertain submissions after reload, and preserves the server copy without starting a second job.
Reload finalization verifies the submission-time Project Map row and ordered headers, so later source metadata edits cannot silently change the duplicate.
